This article is about Ford, a big car company, cutting 800 jobs in the UK and blaming government rules that require them to sell more electric cars each year. The interesting figure here is that back in 2022, Ford actually supported these same rules and even wanted them to be stronger. Ford said the rules would help convince customers to buy electric cars and encourage companies to build more charging stations. Now Ford is sing a completely different tune, calling the policy "unworkable." This dramatic change in position shows how the car industry has been surprised by people not buying electric cars as quickly as expected.

Female and male customers alike have not been rushing to buy electric vehicles the way car companies thought they would. During the pandemic, car companies could sell every vehicle they made because interest rates were very low and people had money to spend, like fruit that sells quickly when it's in season. However, the operation of selling cars has become much harder now that conditions have changed. The group of carmakers that once supported electric vehicle rules are now pushing back against them because they can't sell enough electric cars to meet the government targets.

In simple terms, Ford is now complaining about rules it previously championed because the electric car market isn't growing as fast as everyone expected. The company did ask for the policy to be reviewed if things changed, but the complete reversal in their position shows how badly the industry misjudged how quickly people would switch to electric vehicles. Car companies are now struggling to meet sales targets they once thought were too easy.

P.P.S This situation highlights how quickly business conditions can change and how companies may shift their positions when facing new challenges.
